doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Ken Burns documentary
summary: He saw part of it, liked learning about Armstrong, but wished it had been more balanced.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: You know I didn’t see that whole documentary. I saw some of the early ones and enjoyed learning so much about Louis Armstrong. A lot of stuff I didn’t really know. So I was really pleased and I saw that as a big plus. From talking to my musical colleagues that apparently he left the last 50 years of music history for an hour and a half segment, I didn’t even end up finishing it so I can’t comment on the sweep of the whole work. I guess in his defense he never pretended that this was supposed to be a definitive balanced history of the music, but an evocation of what spoke to him. So Godspeed but from my own purposes, at least what I’ve heard second-hand, I do wish it had been more balanced.
